title: Critères de classification ACR/EULAR 2015 pour la goutte
short_title: Critères de classification ACR/EULAR 2015 de la goutte
formula:
The 2015 ACR/EULAR Classification for Gout is determined by the following criteria:

**Entry Criterion**

≥1 episode of swelling, pain, or tenderness in a peripheral joint/bursa

- If absent, do not classify as gout
- If present, apply sufficient criterion

**Sufficient Criterion**

Presence of monosodium urate (MSU) crystals in a symptomatic joint, bursa, or tophus

- If met, can classify as gout without applying criteria below

**Criteria**

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clinical | | |
| Pattern of joint/bursa involvement during episodes | Joint/bursa other than ankle, midfoot or 1st MTP (or involvement in a polyarthritis) | 0 |
| Ankle OR midfoot (as part of monoarticular/oligoarticular episode without 1st MTP) | 1 | |
| 1st MTP (as part of monoarticular or oligoarticular episode) | 2 | |
| How many of the following characteristics during episode(s)? Erythema overlying joint (reported or observed); can't bear touch or pressure to joint; great difficulty with walking or inability to use joint. | None | 0 |
| One | 1 | |
| Two | 2 | |
| Three | 3 | |
| How many episodes with the following time-course? ≥2 time course symptoms, regardless of anti-inflammatory use: (1) Time to maximal pain <24 hours; (2) Resolution of symptoms in ≤14 days; (3) Complete resolution (to baseline level) between symptomatic episodes. | No typical episodes | 0 |
| One typical episode | 1 | |
| Recurrent typical episodes | 2 | |
| Evidence of tophus 1 | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 4 | |
| Laboratory | | |
| Serum urate 2 | <4 mg/dL [<0.24 mM] | -4 |
| ≥4 or <6 mg/dL [≥0.24 or <0.36 mM] | 0 | |
| ≥6 or <8 mg/dL [≥0.36 or <0.48 mM] | 2 | |
| ≥8 or <10 mg/dL [≥0.48 or <0.60 mM] | 3 | |
| ≥10 mg/dL [≥0.60 mM] | 4 | |
| Synovial fluid analysis of a symptomatic (ever) joint or bursa 3 | Negative for MSU | -2 |
| Not done | 0 | |
| Imaging | | |
| Imaging evidence of urate deposition in symptomatic joint/bursa 4 | Absent or not done | 0 |
| Present | 4 | |
| Imaging evidence of gout-related joint damage 5 | Absent | 0 |
| Present | 4 | |

1. Draining or chalk-like subcutaneous nodule, located in typical locations: joints, ears, olecranon bursae, finger pads, tendons (e.g., Achilles).
2. Measured by uricase method. Ideally scored when patient not taking urate-lowering treatment and patient was >4 weeks from an episode. If practical, retest under those conditions. Highest value irrespective of timing should be used.
3. Should be assessed by a trained observer.
4. Ultrasound: double-contour sign ORDECT: demonstrates urate deposition.
5. X-Ray of hands or feet with ≥1 erosion.

how_to_use.why: - Ces critères peuvent se substituer à l’analyse du liquide synovial (gold standard) si celle-ci n’est pas réalisable, ou si le patient remplit suffisamment d’autres critères.
how_to_use.when: - Patients présentant une mono- ou oligoarthrite d’étiologie indéterminée lorsque la goutte fait partie du diagnostic différentiel.
how_to_use.pearls:
- La classification ACR/EULAR peut être utilisée pour diagnostiquer formellement la goutte.
- Les critères permettent un diagnostic de goutte sans examen synovial (la présence de cristaux d'urate monosodique dans une articulation symptomatique étant le gold standard de la goutte) afin d'aider les cliniciens lorsque l'analyse synoviale n'est pas possible (petite articulation, analyse de laboratoire non disponible).

next_steps.advice:
- Les poussées de goutte sont souvent traitées par une association de corticoïdes, d'AINS (classiquement, l'indométhacine), d'opioïdes pour les douleurs extrêmes et de colchicine, selon l'âge du patient et d'autres facteurs de risque de complications.
- Après la poussée initiale, les patients peuvent bénéficier de traitements hypouricémiants comme l'allopurinol.
next_steps.management: D'autres causes de monoarthrite doivent être envisagées si le patient ne remplit pas les critères de goutte, par exemple : pseudogoutte, arthrite septique, arthrite réactive, arthrite psoriasique, polyarthrite rhumatoïde ou arthrose.

evidence:
- These criteria were developed as a consensus by leading gout experts; interestingly, the criteria were reviewed and agreed upon, then weighted and confirmed in a small set of gout patients.

 - These were then included in a validation larger cohort (the Study for Updated Gout Classification Criteria [SUGAR]).
- The AUC for the ROC for these criteria was 0.95, with a sensitivity of 0.92 and specificity of .89. The clinical-only criteria (without other tests) AUC was 0.89.

instructions: La [Acute Gout Diagnosis Rule](nabda:calc.acute-gout-diagnosis-rule) peut aider à confirmer ou à écarter une goutte, en réduisant la nécessité d’une analyse du liquide synovial chez les patients dont la probabilité est élevée et en encourageant un large diagnostic différentiel chez les patients chez qui la goutte est peu probable.
